name: Demand Indicators
description: The RCI-style demand bars and advisory feed that tell the player what to zone next. Demand is derived, not stored: each bar is a read-model computed from zone vacancy, citizen satisfaction, and tax income, so the indicator can never disagree with the simulation it summarizes — it owns no truth of its own. That is the deliberate design boundary: world.zone_planner owns land use, world.citizen_agent_sim owns population state, economy.currency owns the treasury, and this component only projects their state into a glanceable HUD plus advisory events ('residential demand high', 'power coverage low in district north'). Advisories are throttled and deduplicated because a sim that nags on every tick trains the player to ignore the feed entirely.

inputs.name: demandWindows
inputs.description: The indicator definitions: id, source signals, and thresholds. Ships as R/C/I by default but is data-driven so a farming sim can show crop demand instead.

inputs.name: advisoryCooldownSeconds
inputs.description: Minimum time before the same advisory may repeat. The difference between a helpful advisor and noise.

inputs.name: smoothingFactor
inputs.description: Exponential smoothing applied to bar movement so a single arrival or departure does not make the UI lurch. 0 is raw values, 1 is frozen.

outputs.name: demandLevels
outputs.description: Current value per demand indicator in [-1, 1]: negative is oversupply, positive is unmet demand.

outputs.name: activeAdvisories
outputs.description: Advisories currently in effect with severity and the signal that raised them, so the UI can deep-link 'click to see the problem district'.
